sections.overview: Enallagma signatum is an eastern North American bluet whose mature males are conspicuously orange.
sections.identification: Adults are 25–38 mm; males have orange eyes and thorax and a black abdomen banded orange, while females vary in color.
sections.habitat: It uses lakes, ponds and slow streams with floating plants, especially water lilies.
sections.diet: The accounts consulted provide no prey list specific to this species.
sections.behavior: Illinois observations note activity near dusk and paired flight by the water.
sections.reproduction: Males accompany females as they lay eggs in aquatic plants.
sections.ecology: Compare Enallagma annexum and E. carunculatum: mature E. signatum males are orange.
sections.conservation: The Illinois Department of Natural Resources describes it as common and native in Illinois; that state-level account is not a global population assessment.
